
QUERY-BOTTLENECKS
Identify bottleneck work units blocking the most downstream work (2+ blocked work units)

WHEN TO USE
  Use this command to identify critical path blockers that are preventing progress on multiple work units. Essential for prioritization decisions and unblocking parallelizable work. Run daily during active development to maximize throughput.

PREREQUISITES
  • spec/work-units.json exists with work units and dependency relationships

USAGE
  fspec query-bottlenecks [options]

OPTIONS
  --output <format>
    Output format: text or json
    Default: text

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Daily Prioritization
    Example: # Morning standup: identify blockers
fspec query-bottlenecks

# Prioritize highest score bottleneck
fspec update-work-unit-status AUTH-001 implementing

# After completion
fspec update-work-unit-status AUTH-001 done

# Re-check for new bottlenecks
fspec query-bottlenecks
    undefined

  • Automation with JSON Output
    Example: # Export bottlenecks for dashboard
fspec query-bottlenecks --output json > bottlenecks.json

# Process with jq (highest score first)
jq '.bottlenecks | sort_by(-.score) | .[0]' bottlenecks.json
    undefined

  • Team Coordination
    Example: # Identify parallelizable work
fspec query-bottlenecks

# If bottleneck score is high (5+), assign multiple team members:
# - Member 1: Complete bottleneck AUTH-001
# - Member 2-4: Work on unblocked parallel tasks

# After bottleneck complete, previously blocked work can proceed
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. Run bottleneck query: fspec query-bottlenecks → 2. Prioritize highest-score bottleneck → 3. Complete bottleneck work unit → 4. Update status: fspec update-work-unit-status <id> done → 5. Re-run query to identify next bottleneck

EXAMPLES
  1. List bottleneck work units blocking 2+ work units
  $ fspec query-bottlenecks
  Bottleneck Work Units (blocking 2+ work units):

AUTH-001 (implementing) - Setup authentication infrastructure
  Bottleneck Score: 5
  Direct Blocks: AUTH-002, AUTH-003
  Transitive Blocks: AUTH-004, AUTH-005, AUTH-006

DB-001 (testing) - Database schema migration
  Bottleneck Score: 3
  Direct Blocks: DB-002, DB-003, DB-004

Total bottlenecks: 2

  2. Output bottlenecks as JSON for automation
  $ fspec query-bottlenecks --output json
  {
  "bottlenecks": [
    {
      "id": "AUTH-001",
      "title": "Setup authentication infrastructure",
      "status": "implementing",
      "score": 5,
      "directBlocks": ["AUTH-002", "AUTH-003"],
      "transitiveBlocks": ["AUTH-004", "AUTH-005", "AUTH-006"]
    }
  ]
}

  3. Show only top bottlenecks (highest scores)
  $ fspec query-bottlenecks | head -20
  Bottleneck Work Units (blocking 2+ work units):

AUTH-001 (implementing) - Setup authentication infrastructure
  Bottleneck Score: 5
  Direct Blocks: AUTH-002, AUTH-003
  Transitive Blocks: AUTH-004, AUTH-005, AUTH-006

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Error: No bottlenecks found
    Fix: No work units are blocking 2+ other work units. This is good - no major blockers exist.

  ✗ Error: work-units.json not found
    Fix: Run: fspec init to create work-units.json file

  ✗ Error: Invalid work-units.json format
    Fix: Check for JSON syntax errors. Run: fspec validate-work-units (if available)

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec query-orphans
  fspec suggest-dependencies
  fspec add-dependency
  fspec update-work-unit-status
  fspec show-work-unit

NOTES
  • Bottleneck score = total work units blocked (direct + transitive)
  • Only work units NOT in "done" or "blocked" status are considered bottlenecks
  • Minimum bottleneck score is 2 (blocking at least 2 work units)
  • Work units are ranked by score (highest to lowest)
  • Transitive blocks = work units blocked indirectly through dependency chain
  • Direct blocks = work units directly blocked by this work unit
  • Completing a high-score bottleneck can unblock significant parallelizable work
